text:
Ravi: Heads-up — after yesterday's tweak to reduce micro-batch interval to 3ms we saw a small but consistent perf regression on some mid-tail workloads. p50 fine, p95 up ~18% and throughput down ~9% in the canary. Profile attached below.

Lena: ack. can you paste the quick profile numbers? was kernel selection different? :eyes:

Ravi: quick excerpt: kernel selector moved a subset of sequences from fp16-gemm -> int8-fallback path when avg seq_len drifted up ~6 tokens. KV cache miss-rate jumped from 6.3% -> 18.1% for that trace. micro-batch sizes showing heavier skew (lots of size 1/2 and a few 12s).

Sam: micro-batch interval to 3ms was our low-latency push. That increases coalesce churn. If arrival variance spikes we end up emitting small batches quickly which reduces effective KV reuse.

Nia: sounds like two coupled issues: coalesce delay reduction + lack of jitter -> deterministic small batches, and kernel selection reacting to slightly longer sequences. if KV miss rises, token budget gating doesn't help because fewer tokens per batch.

Matt: what does queue occupancy look like? any queue-side starvation or head-of-line blocking?

Ravi: queue hist: 60% of windows emitted with batch_size <=2, tail 4% >10. Latency SLOs satisfied for p50 but costs increased. Kernel switch triggered by per-request "prefetch_priming" heuristic that checks aggregate seq distribution over the last 2s window.

Lena: recommended quick mitigations: bump coalesce_delay back to 6ms, reintroduce small uniform jitter (0-2ms) so we don't synchronise, and temporarily relax kernel selection threshold (e.g., require +10 tokens longer average before switching).

Sam: agree. Also try raising TargetTokenBudget from 32->48 in canary so that batches accumulate a bit more before emission. Could be a cheap win.

Nia: adding an experiment matrix:
- A: coalesce_delay=6ms, jitter=0-2ms, token_budget=32, kernel_threshold=default
- B: coalesce_delay=6ms, jitter=0-2ms, token_budget=48, kernel_threshold=default
- C: coalesce_delay=3ms, jitter=0-2ms, token_budget=48, kernel_threshold=+10tok bias

Matt: and capture these metrics per-variant: batch_size_hist, kv_miss_rate, kernel_variant_share, p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec.

infra-bot: started canary run for experiment B on pool:dedicated-canary-7 (build 3423). Logs: https://ci.redwood/3423 :robot_face:

Ravi: quick perf snippet for the failing trace (log):
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] emit_window id=0x7f23 size=1 seq_mean=18.2 kernel=fp16->int8_fallback kv_hit=false
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] emit_window id=0x7f28 size=1 seq_mean=17.9 kernel=fp16->int8_fallback kv_hit=false
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] emit_window id=0x7f3a size=12 seq_mean=21.3 kernel=fp16_gemm kv_hit=true
```

Nia: that pattern (many small windows + occasional bigger windows) is classic for synchronization without jitter. Kernel selector sees the occasional long windows and flips heuristics for safety; but small windows lose KV priming.

Sam: timeline: implement A/B within 2h, run 30m steady-state traffic per variant, then compare. also run micro-profiling for kernel selector decision path (log levels).

Lena: if B reduces kv_miss <10% and p95 back to baseline we'd roll it to canary pools. If not, consider adding a short-lived KV prefetch op for small windows (cheap prewarm for the next token).

Matt: note — prefetch increases memory traffic; gate it behind token_budget < X and only on fp16_gemm candidates.

Ravi: will run the three variants, capture metrics Matt listed, and post results here. thanks team. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary B finished: 30m run completed. summary: kv_miss=7.4%, p95 delta = +2%, throughput -1.8%. Full logs -> https://ci.redwood/3423/results

Nia: that looks promising for B. let's wait for A and C but good sign — jitter + larger budget seems to recover KV reuse without reverting micro-batch latency goals.

Sam: followup action items: (1) roll coalesce_delay=6ms + jitter=0-2ms to canary pools; (2) schedule kernel-threshold tuning RFC to avoid flip-flop on occasional tails; (3) investigate small-window prefetch as fallback.

Ravi: created a short runbook note in the ops doc: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/coalesce-kv-2026 — includes safe rollback commands.

Lena: thanks — will take point on the RFC.

Matt: tagging infra folks to watch canary: @Sam @Nia @Ravi :rocket:
